bugs.error_message: WorkflowExecutor.lua:1057: attempt to compare boolean <= number
bugs.root_cause: Lua short-circuit evaluation: when curStep.isSyncSource == false, isSyncStep = false, then `ordinal = false and ...` evaluates to false (not nil). `required = false and ...` also evaluates to false. Then `leaderExec.currentStep >= false` crashes because Lua implements >= as b <= a, hitting `false <= number`.
bugs.fix: Added `or nil` to both `ordinal` and `required` local variable assignments to ensure they are nil (not false) when the short-circuit produces a falsy boolean.

bugs.error_message: goToPreviousStep/goToNextStep leaves follower in STATUS_WAITING_FOR_LEADER, executeCurrentStep never called
bugs.root_cause: `wasPaused` only captured STATUS_PAUSED, so the status-reset guard missed STATUS_WAITING_FOR_LEADER. After manual navigation the follower kept its old status and the `if status == RUNNING` guard blocked executeCurrentStep.
bugs.fix: Changed both goToPreviousStep and goToNextStep to reset status to RUNNING when `wasPaused OR status == STATUS_WAITING_FOR_LEADER` (manual navigation always resumes).

bugs.error_message: CP refill cycle broken: after running out of consumables CP triggers AD but AD does not auto-start CP on return
bugs.root_cause: Refactor removed setStartHelper(true) entirely. Without it, when CP internally starts AD for a refill run, AD finishes and WM's cpHandedOffToAD path sees neither CP nor AD running and marks the step complete prematurely.
bugs.fix: Re-introduced ADIntegration:setStartCPOnCompletion(vehicle, true) in startCourseplayStep (after CP starts), and ADIntegration:clearCPHandoff(vehicle) in startAutoDriveStep (to prevent WM-directed AD steps from accidentally auto-starting CP). Also added cpHandedOffWait grace counter (2 polls) so the brief gap between AD finishing and CP restarting doesn't trigger premature completion.

bugs.error_message: After save/reload, follower vehicle that was WAITING_FOR_LEADER at step 1 advances to step 2 instead of waiting
bugs.root_cause: AD saves stateModule:setActive(true) across game reloads, so the dummy AD hold (used to keep AD alive while follower waits for leader) persists after reload. onPostLoad always restored status as PAUSED. The auto-resume path (checking adRunning) detected the dummy hold as real AD activity, transitioned follower to RUNNING+waitingForCompletion without going through executeCurrentStep, bypassing the leader-sync check entirely. AD then had no real route and fired onADFinishedEvent almost immediately, triggering onStepCompleted → step 2.
bugs.fix: Save #status attribute in saveToXMLFile when status == WAITING_FOR_LEADER. In onPostLoad, read #status and restore WAITING_FOR_LEADER exactly (no autoResumeUntil, dummyHelperActive=true). Auto-resume only triggers for STATUS_PAUSED so it never fires. The update-loop WAITING_FOR_LEADER poll correctly re-checks the leader condition each tick.

bugs.error_message: After save/reload, follower in WAITING_FOR_LEADER state has AD auto-start driving
bugs.root_cause: stateModule:setActive(true) (dummy hold) persisted by AD across saves. On reload AD auto-resumes the last route, causing the follower to drive. Additionally, FS25 sleeps distant vehicles without an active AI helper, so the dummy MUST call setActive(true) to keep WM's update loop running.
bugs.fix: onPostLoad: for WAITING_FOR_LEADER restores, call setActive(false) to clear AD's auto-started route, then setActive(true) to re-apply clean dummy hold; set dummyHelperActive=true. startDummyADHold renamed to startDummyHold, now takes vehicle param, calls stateModule:setActive(true) directly. stopCurrentStep and pauseWorkflow call setActive(false) to deactivate. No gate in update loop — leader poll always runs when in WAITING_FOR_LEADER.

bugs.error_message: clearCPHandoff not called when startRoute fails — setStartHelper(true) left armed from prior CP step
bugs.root_cause: ADIntegration:clearCPHandoff was inside the 'if success then' branch of startAutoDriveStep. If startRoute returned false, StartDriving was never called (so AD did not internally reset the flag), leaving setStartHelper(true) from the prior CP step armed. Any subsequent AD activation (manual or retry) would then auto-start CP — the AD→CP double-start / 13-second crash.
bugs.fix: Moved clearCPHandoff to before the startRoute call (unconditional). On success, StartDriving resets the flag internally anyway, so calling clear first is idempotent. On failure, the flag is now always disarmed.

bugs.error_message: User report: 'the Steyer tractor lost its leader' — follower permanently stuck in waiting_for_leader with leaderVehicle=nil after reload
bugs.root_cause: Leader identity was persisted as leaderVehicleXmlIndex, a positional index parsed from savegame.key ("vehicles.vehicle(N)"). This index is only stable within one load — across separate save sessions, buying/selling a vehicle (or any change to vehicles.xml composition/order) shifts every later index. Log evidence: STEYR 'Absolut 6280 CVT' saved leaderVehicleXmlIndex=199 pointing to '8R 410' in one session; on the next load, xmlIndex 199 resolved to a completely different vehicle ('IDEAL 10T', which has no workflow at all), so tryResolvePendingLeader could never match it and the follower stayed blocked forever.
bugs.fix: Added leaderVehicleUniqueId, persisted/matched via the vehicle's own engine-assigned uniqueId (vehicle.uniqueId, also visible as the uniqueId="..." attribute on <vehicle> in vehicles.xml) instead of a positional index. uniqueId does not shift when other vehicles are added/removed/reordered. Kept leaderVehicleXmlIndex/legacy leaderVehicleIndex/leaderWorkflowId as read-only fallback for saves written before this fix. New pendingLeaderUniqueId field mirrors the existing pendingLeaderXmlIndex/pendingLeaderWorkflowId deferred-resolution mechanism in WorkflowExecutor.lua (tryResolvePendingLeader, isLeaderSyncSatisfied).
